diagnostic.title: Startup Diagnostics
diagnostic.reloadHelp: Reloading retries the renderer only. If the backend binary or Python process is still unhealthy, restart the full app after addressing the issue shown above.
diagnostic.actionState.exportUnavailable: Support-bundle export is not available in this environment.
diagnostic.actionState.pathUnavailable: {label} is not available for this failure.
diagnostic.actionState.revealUnavailable: Path reveal is not available in this environment.
diagnostic.reason.binary_not_found.title: Backend binary was not found
diagnostic.reason.binary_not_found.descr: The packaged backend executable is missing or was removed after installation.
diagnostic.reason.binary_not_found.nextS: Reinstall the app or restore the backend binary from the installer.
diagnostic.reason.binary_permission_deni: The operating system blocked execution permissions for the backend process.
Check file permissions and retry after reinstalling the app.
diagnostic.reason.port_in_use.title: Preferred startup port was unavailable
diagnostic.reason.port_in_use.descriptio: Another process is already using the default backend port.
diagnostic.reason.port_in_use.nextStep: Close the conflicting process or restart the app to retry on a new port.
diagnostic.reason.python_error.title: Backend crashed during startup
diagnostic.reason.python_error.descripti: The Python backend exited before it reported readiness.
diagnostic.reason.python_error.nextStep: Review the technical details below and fix the backend error before retrying.
diagnostic.reason.startup_timeout.title: Backend startup timed out
diagnostic.reason.startup_timeout.descri: The backend process did not report readiness within the startup timeout window.
diagnostic.reason.startup_timeout.nextSt: Retry after checking local security software and Python dependency health.
diagnostic.reason.antivirus_blocked.desc: The backend appears to have been blocked by Windows Defender or another security product.
diagnostic.reason.antivirus_blocked.next: Allow the DS Agent backend and retry the app.
diagnostic.reason.crash_loop.title: Backend entered a crash loop
diagnostic.reason.crash_loop.description: Multiple startup attempts failed before the backend became healthy.
diagnostic.reason.crash_loop.nextStep: Use the diagnostic details below to identify the repeated startup failure.
diagnostic.reason.health_check_failed.de: The backend emitted READY but did not answer the health check successfully.
diagnostic.reason.health_check_failed.ne: Check for partial startup failures or port binding issues in the diagnostic log.
diagnostic.reason.fallback.title: Backend startup failed
diagnostic.reason.fallback.description: The desktop app could not establish a healthy backend process.
diagnostic.reason.fallback.nextStep: Review the diagnostic details below before retrying.
diagnostic.recovery.antivirus_blocked.he: Restore the backend from security quarantine
diagnostic.recovery.antivirus_blocked.wi: Open Windows Security, then go to Virus & threat protection and Protection history.
Restore or allow the DS Agent backend executable, then add an exclusion for its install folder if it is quarantined repeatedly.
Restart DS Agent. If startup still fails, export the support bundle and attach it when escalating.
diagnostic.recovery.antivirus_blocked.ge: Open your endpoint security or antivirus product and check whether the DS Agent backend executable was quarantined.
Allow the executable or add an exclusion for its install folder.
Restart DS Agent and export the support bundle if the block continues.
diagnostic.recovery.antivirus_blocked.no: Use the buttons below to reveal the backend location and logs folder directly.
diagnostic.recovery.binary_not_found.hea: Repair or reinstall the packaged backend
diagnostic.recovery.binary_not_found.ste: Close DS Agent completely before reinstalling or restoring files.
Reveal the backend location and confirm that the packaged executable exists in the ds-agent-backend folder.
If the file is missing, reinstall from a fresh installer and then retry the app.
diagnostic.recovery.binary_not_found.not: If the file was removed by security software, follow the antivirus flow after reinstalling.
diagnostic.recovery.binary_permission_de: Reveal the backend location and check whether the executable is blocked, quarantined, or missing execute permission.
If your OS or security tool exposes an Unblock or Allow action, apply it to the backend executable.
Restart DS Agent after permissions are restored.
diagnostic.recovery.port_in_use.heading: Clear repeated port conflicts
diagnostic.recovery.port_in_use.step1: Close any duplicate DS Agent instances or stale backend processes.
diagnostic.recovery.port_in_use.step2: If the failure repeats, inspect what is binding port {port} and stop the conflicting process.
diagnostic.recovery.port_in_use.step3: Start DS Agent again. The app can fall back to another port, but repeated conflicts should still be investigated.
Export the support bundle so the startup handshake and follow-up health failure are captured together.
Review the stderr summary and recent logs for import errors, port bind issues, or immediate shutdown after READY.
Retry the app after addressing the failing dependency or environment issue.
diagnostic.recovery.startup_timeout.head: Narrow down a slow or blocked startup
diagnostic.recovery.startup_timeout.step: Reveal the logs folder and check whether the backend is starting slowly, blocked by security software, or waiting on an unavailable dependency.
Export the support bundle before retrying so the timeout context is preserved.
Restart the app after addressing the blocking condition.
diagnostic.recovery.python_error.heading: Fix the backend error before retrying
diagnostic.recovery.python_error.step1: Read the stderr summary and technical details for the first concrete Python or dependency error.
diagnostic.recovery.python_error.step2: Reveal the logs folder and export the support bundle so the failing startup path is preserved.
diagnostic.recovery.python_error.step3: Retry the app only after the root cause is fixed.
diagnostic.recovery.crash_loop.heading: Stop the repeated startup failure loop
diagnostic.recovery.crash_loop.step1: Export the support bundle so all recent startup attempts are captured in one artifact.
diagnostic.recovery.crash_loop.step2: Use the technical details and logs to identify what is crashing the backend before it stabilizes.
diagnostic.recovery.crash_loop.step3: If the backend executable is missing or quarantined, use the recovery buttons below before retrying.
diagnostic.recovery.fallback.heading: Collect context before retrying
diagnostic.recovery.fallback.step1: Export the support bundle so the current startup failure state is preserved.
diagnostic.recovery.fallback.step2: Review the diagnostic details and logs for the first actionable error.
diagnostic.recovery.fallback.step3: Retry the app after the underlying issue is addressed.
